A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CTBench. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material across appendix moves and renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original benchmark results in Table 1, model-property and corruption analyses, and three-seed results and architecture comparisons in Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 retains these original results and adds regularization ablations, instability-bound comparisons, cross-architecture shared-error results and certification-method comparisons.

M1.justification: The implemented training algorithms, unified loss, batch-normalization fixes, architectures and weight-averaging procedure are retained. V4 expands explanations and evaluates additional configurations without introducing a new method component or changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, CIFAR-10, TinyImageNet, MNIST-C and CIFAR-10-C under the same represented tasks and perturbation coverage. The added analyses reuse this coverage. Other norms and synthetic datasets appear only in discussion of prior work.

E2.justification: V4 Table 4 adds a numerical comparison with Adaptive Randomized Smoothing using results attributed to Lyu et al. (2024). Table 22 adds standalone IBP and CROWN-IBP certification comparisons against MN-BAB. The main benchmark's eight training methods remain unchanged.

E3.justification: V4 adds reported evaluation designs involving zero-L1 controls, separate incomplete-certifier evaluations and CNN5–CNN7 shared-error comparisons. The original benchmark splits, metrics, perturbation radii, training schedules and 1000-second certification timeout remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 substantially expands supporting analyses through L1 ablations, regularization-dependent robustness–accuracy curves, sampling-versus-IBP instability comparisons, shared mistakes across architectures and incomplete-versus-complete certification. These additions test questions beyond the retained architecture, verifier-overlap and model-property analyses.

E5.justification: The three-seed means and standard deviations in v3 Tables 9–13 are retained unchanged as v4 Tables 13–17. The fixed-seed statement and independence-based expected mistake counts also remain. New instability bounds do not introduce confidence intervals or a changed sampling estimator.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and matched appendix scores remain unchanged, but v4 adds substantial result sets for the new analyses. For example, Table 22 newly reports MTL-IBP certified accuracy of 0.62% with IBP and 23.31% with CROWN-IBP, alongside the retained 64.41% MN-BAB result. These are comparisons between certification methods, not performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: V4 Appendix C.6 adds analytical per-batch training-cost formulas in Table 11, parameterized by attack steps, class count and network-split costs. V3 reported measured runtimes but lacked this systematic analytical accounting. Existing robustness definitions and training objectives are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, retaining the unified benchmark contribution, improved literature comparisons and five model-property insights. The introduction and conclusion preserve the same substantive contributions; added supporting evidence does not redefine them.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands applicability and interpretation discussions: Section 6 qualifies the absence of other-norm methods as an absence of scalable methods, while Appendix B discusses non-ReLU limitations, local versus global corruption failures, regularization trade-offs and context-dependent utilization. It also strengthens the interpretation of shared mistakes using cross-architecture evidence.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies that the retained CNN5 comparison applies CNN7-tuned hyperparameters to both implementations, and the added ablation table documents tested L1 weights. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware specifications, measured runtimes and code/checkpoint access information are retained.

R1.justification: V4 develops positioning against randomized smoothing and L2 deterministic certification in Section 6 and Appendices B.3–B.4, and distinguishes its instability analysis from Shi et al. (2021) in B.7. Together with newly cited work, these passages substantially expand the justification of scope and relationships to alternative approaches.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained, with local editing and explanatory refinements. V4 revises Appendix A, inserts an Additional Discussions appendix, renumbers the existing appendices and adds acknowledgements, an impact statement and publication details.

P2.justification: V4 adds six tables and two figures, including new analysis displays and Figure 8's visualization of existing Table 1 results. It also enlarges Table 1 and several retained figures and changes their placement, producing a substantial visual presentation revision.

improvement.justification: V4 makes the existing benchmark easier to assess through regularization ablations, explicit certification-method results and checks on the instability estimate. Larger displays and more specific applicability discussions also help. These are useful, targeted improvements, while the important difficulty of separating implementation gains from hyperparameter tuning remains acknowledged in Appendix A.
